utterances.text: Okay. To the extent that there were these designations, sir, it there were certainly a hierarchy, if you will, will you agree with me on that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move ahead, then, to your page 6647, 7581 of the English version. This is a decision again September, 1992, edition of the official gazette, decision on -- if we can put the English on the ELMO, English page 7581, just a few pages after the first one. I've got it here. I can hand it to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I have it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a decision on ranks, the awarding of ranks, promotion to higher rank, again laying out a number of ranks for different levels, non-commissioned officers, soldiers, officers. Now, sir, doesn't this contradict your testimony earlier that there were no ranks and that ranks had not been published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: It does not contradict my earlier testimony because I said that ranks were not assigned to soldiers, they were not assigned. This is just the law on ranks which provides for the future organisation and establishing and what ranks to be eventually assigned in the HVO but this came into force on -- in 1994, not earlier, because if the President appoints somebody as general, the official gazette will publish the name of that person and it will say, [redacted], by the decision of the president, is appointed and given the rank of a general. That's what it would have to say. This is just the provisions of the law, because previously, the Serbian language was used and this law, and then it has been changed and as such, published with new titles, new terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So again, we do have a publication from 1992 which does give authority and allows for the assignment of ranks to all levels within the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I have never read these official gazettes, that was not my obligation, but in practice, there were no ranks, and as for the Official Gazette, that may have been the case. Somebody may have been appointed, but in Siroki Brijeg, nobody was officially commissioned because the Defence office has never received such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, though, that the assigning of ranks was a matter that would have fallen within the competence of the military side of the HVO? Outside the competence, for example, of the Defence office of the HVO in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Military component could not assign ranks. One unit can propose or issue a request to the ministry for a higher rank for a promotion. That was in 1994, when ranks were assigned as per previous merits. So it could not have been a military unit either. It could just send a request to the ministry and if it was a lower rank, then the ministry could deal with that itself. If it was a higher level ranking officer, then it would have to be the President. And the lower ranks are not published in the official gazette, just the highest ranks have to be publicised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll break. We'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After you cautioned me strongly that I should wait for the witness to leave before I object, now I don't know what to do, but just for the record, P6 -- 016.1, in the description it says in handwriting it says Tuta's Brigade. I inspected the document. It doesn't say that anywhere. If you look at the document 606.21, can you please look at the Croatian text and tell us what it says in the Croatian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can speed this up, the document wasn't referred to in the cross-examination and it's not being tendered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, did you hear the statement by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. I just wanted to object for the record, in principle, because this is not a small matter. In the same way I objected to, in principle, to the previous translation, because it says here clear and loud, and our interpreters can check that, it says in handwriting, "With the brigade and Tuta." And in the translation, it says, "Tuta's brigade." A major difference, I would say, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The document isn't in evidence but if you direct us to it, it says "drives question mark trailer truck to brigade, and Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says clearly here that somebody is driving a trailer to the brigade and to Tuta. So it is not Tuta but to Tuta. But let's not waste any more time. I just wanted to say that for the record. It says -- it can be checked by the interpreters in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, if you have some objections to a certain document, you ever the full right to do that, but you do that when the witness has left the courtroom and when we have those documents tendered into evidence. You may raise your objections to any documents. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You're right. Sometimes I really should count to five before I start doing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like to ask you now is the following: For example, document 558.3, and the first question: Would a document that has your name printed out -- would it have to be signed either you or a person authorised by you? Would it have to bear a stamp in order to be considered a valid document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Object to the leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it is a leading question, and this issue has been mentioned in your direct examination, and as well as in the cross-examination. You may put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'll help you, Mr. Krsnik, ask the witness how is a document validated in your office?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You've heard the question. Can you please answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes. In order to be validated, the document has to be signed by me, has to be validated by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how do you validate it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I stamp it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does this document bear your signature and stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's move on. Please can you tell the Chamber whether you know somebody who refers to himself or who is referred to as Colonel Cavar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who is that person, can you tell the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Colonel Cavar was the commander of the Siroki Brijeg Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you: Have you ever seen an identity card of the Siroki Brijeg Brigade by any of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when it says the designation of the unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so, Mr. Krsnik, unless your question will lead to something that is mentioned in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Siroki Brijeg Brigade has been mentioned. We have talked about it, Your Honours. I just want to ask the witness whether, on the identity card held by the soldiers, what did it say on the ID card? What was the name of the brigade on that card.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object on the grounds it's beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may ask what this brigade is called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I put the question in this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How was the brigade referred to in the soldiers' booklet or ID card in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: It was denoted as the Siroki Brijeg Brigade. It did not have any other name. That was its name, the Siroki Brijeg Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What were the initials? Can you tell us what was its abbreviated name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: We did not have any initials. They were not used in official documents. What it had to say was the Siroki Brijeg Brigade in full letters, full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. Please tell me, this is my last question, the decisions on disability that the Prosecutor was examining you about, did you check the place of wounding and the affiliation to various units? Were there any abuses of these documents, all these documents refer to 1995, 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: There were a lot of abuses I'm embarrassed to admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe it's a suggestive or leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it's very suggestive. We just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But the witness has answered that question, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Judges? Yes, Judge Clark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness, I think you're NQ. Is that the pseudonym that you have, NQ? Nobody gave a pseudonym. It is? Okay. Witness NQ, in relation to the last question that Mr. Krsnik asked you about the identity cards of soldiers, my understanding of what you said is that all conscripts in Siroki Brijeg were described as belonging to the Siroki Brijeg Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No. There were conscripts from Siroki Brijeg in other units which did not belong to the area of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm talking about people that were with in your jurisdiction, conscripts within your jurisdiction. Were they -- are you saying that the only unit which existed, that you took care of, was the Siroki Brijeg Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: There was the Siroki Brijeg Brigade, and the Convicts Battalion within the Siroki Brijeg Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And did you have a home guard brigade unit and a military police unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Later on, after the re-establishment, yes, there was a home guard brigade -- unit. The military police did not exist. It was -- there was a unit whose command was in Ljubuski but it was one unit for the entire area of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We've heard evidence from witnesses about the presence of military police in Siroki Brijeg. In fact I think they had a headquarters or an office there, and we've also heard about home guard looking after prisoners. Are you saying that this evidence is incorrect, that there were no military police and no home guard in Siroki Brijeg in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: This is not what I said. There were military policemen from Siroki Brijeg but it was just a squad but the command of the military police was in Ljubuski, later on in Mostar, and they sent, this military police unit to Siroki Brijeg. They were not from Siroki Brijeg but our conscripts, who replenished the military police units, they were sent to Grude and those from Grude, for example they would be sent to Siroki Brijeg. It was easier for them to work if they didn't know the people there. And the home guards were the elderly people who were not sent to the ground, who remained in Siroki Brijeg. This is the people who we call -- refer to as home guard. They were engaged in doing some works there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So you agree with me they certainly existed and there must have been some sort of administrative machinery to call those people up for duties as home guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you have a counterpart in the town of Siroki Brijeg who was actually the HVO military defence department attache, if I can call him that, your military counterpart, in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I'm not too clear on your question. There was just one Defence office, and that was a civilian institution. And as for the military part, the command had its offices which served the purposes of the brigade, which were used to serve the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, who was the person who would have been the military counterpart in the HVO of your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know the name. These people changed very often, and I wouldn't be able to give you any names. There was the person in the brigade who was in charge of the written documents for that brigade, and I really don't know what the name of that person was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges questions? Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I do wish to continue along the lines of the Honourable Judge Clark's questions. I think that the question was misunderstood by the witness. You correct me, Your Honour, if I'm wrong, but who is the supreme military commander in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: The top military commander was the commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Pero Cavar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, when you say brigade, in the military chain of command, who was a brigade responsible to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: To the sector, I think. I'm not very familiar with the military hierarchy, I am with the civilian hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If were you in charge of the civilian parts of the HVO, as regards military matters, is the commander of the Siroki Brijeg your counterpart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who is, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: My counterpart is the head of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Pero Cavar, was he in a military sense your counterpart in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Oh, that, yes, yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If this is viewed as being a little bit beyond the scope of Judge Clark's question then I'll sit down. It's a bit related to Judge Clark's question and then the question from Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion, the KB, if it was an independent unit for special purposes, did it exist in a different hierarchy or chain of command, different from that for the Siroki Brijeg Battalion itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No. It was within the Siroki Brijeg Brigade. It was also commanded by Pero Cavar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what an independent units for special purposes is, within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Well, precisely -- well, not really. I can't really tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, the photograph P26.2 as marked by the witness on direct examination, we'd ask that that be admitted. And I think the number might -- maybe Ms. Thompson can help us D1/401, as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. marked? That would be the only document that we would ask to be tendered through this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So this document, D1/401 is admitted into evidence. And on your side, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we had also the witness marking on a different photograph which was 26.9. So we would offer that. In addition, there are I think about seven documents which I can identify at this time. I'm not offering all of the documents that were on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you'll submit us in written form, at a later stage. Are there any objections to that document P26.9?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not the photograph as marked. We have no objection to that. And we will look at the written submission on the other documents, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, so this document is admitted into the evidence. Yes, Mr. Krsnik, are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, as until now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. So we'll have the next witness. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the next witness, please? Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President while we are bringing the next witness in, could we go to -- I didn't realise it would be so quick. If we could go to private session just for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, sir, I know that you have an eye problem but --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. You're going to get a piece of paper now from the usher and your name and surname are on that piece of paper, and if it is indeed so, just say yes. Can I tell you one more thing? Can you follow this transcript in front of you, this text on the monitor? When you see this black dot that is moving, don't give an answer. When it stops, when the typing stops, then start giving your answer. We had problems with your previous witnesses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The most important is for you to wait for a few seconds after I finish my question so that our interpreters could interpret everything. So is this your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, this is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. So let us proceed now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, what's -- what's his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please without stating your name, please introduce yourself briefly to the Honourable Trial Chamber, where do you live, where you completed school, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [no interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I was born on the 1st of January, 1967, in Siroki Brijeg. I completed elementary school and high school in Siroki Brijeg. That is where I live and work today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I will be dealing with 1993 only, because the Trial Chamber has heard a lot of evidence about 1992. So very briefly, in 1992, did you join the defence in any way, I mean the defence of Siroki Brijeg. If so, tell us which units, when but just give us a very brief answer to my questions, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: In 1992, I joined the Crisis Staff of Siroki Brijeg. As for the shelling of Siroki Brijeg, in the beginning of April, I joined the Convicts Battalion and we were liberating Siroki Brijeg, both on the left and right bank of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Also very briefly, were you a volunteer in 1991 at the theatres of war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer it was overlapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So when were you returned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the interpreters did not catch up with you. Would you please ask your question once again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, we really have to pay attention. I have to pay more attention than you because I'm a professional as opposed to you. So how long were you in Croatia, in -- at the front line in Croatia and then when did you return to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: On the 1st of July, 1991, I joined the defence of the Republic of Croatia, and I was there until February, 1992, when I returned to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go on. Please tell me in 1992, were you in the Convicts Battalion all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I was in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I stayed in the Convicts Battalion until the end of June. Then I got orders to establish the anti-terrorist group Baja Kraljevic, [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who issued this order to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: The Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, in this courtroom, we heard that Baja Kraljevic was an integral part of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Baja Kraljevic was never part of the Convicts Battalion, ever since it was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Honourable Trial Chamber what kind after military unit this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: This was a professional unit, under the direct command of the Main Staff. Apart from the Main Staff, nobody else had the right to issue any orders to it or to give it any assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, I was not careful. Well, there is no excuse. I mean if I just say I'm tired. The transcript does include now which position the witness held. So could we please have that redacted? And I'm asking you, Witness, not to say anything that would identify you because we are going to ask for private session when you refer to matters like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you say who your immediate commander was, your immediate superior in terms of Baja Kraljevic, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: My immediate commander was exclusively the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In 1993, did you get orders from anyone except for the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: From no one else, no one but the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Honourable Trial Chamber until when your unit existed and if you know, for how long did the Convicts Battalion exist? For how long did you exist as such units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: The ATG Baja Kraljevic existed until the end of November or rather December, 1992 and the Convicts Battalion, and then they joined the professional brigade, the 2nd Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We have a mistake in the transcript. It says 1992 and I asked you explicitly about which year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: It is the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Therefore, can you clarify to this Trial Chamber when the ATG Baja Kraljevic formally ceased to exist or, if you know, when the Convicts Battalion ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: They ceased to exist on the 1st of January, 1994, when they were transferred to the 1st Battalion of the 2nd Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, could you break that question up into two? When did the Baja Kraljevic cease to exist and when did the Convicts Battalion? Because they are being rolled up and then who became part of the 2nd Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You heard the question, please, so could you give a detailed answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Both units, the Convicts Battalion and the ATG, became part of the 1st Battalion of the 2nd Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they cease to exist at the same time or did one cease to exist earlier and the other one later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1993, the re-establishment was carried out and most of the units were transferred to guards brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Please where did you live in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: In 1993, I lived in Siroki Brijeg and I worked in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know about the chain of command or who the commander of the Convicts Battalion was in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: After my friend Cikota was killed, General Andabak was commander, and also there was the commander on the ground, Zeljko Vukoja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Andabak, and you said general. When did he get the rank of general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: At that time, there weren't any ranks but that's what we called each other, generals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We heard evidence in this courtroom that he was an alcoholic. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Andabak was not an alcoholic. He had severe diabetes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please can you tell the Trial Chamber whether it is correct to say that the aim of the Convicts Battalion was to expel Muslims from the areas where there was fighting during 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No. That was not the aim, to expel the Muslims. The aim was to defend oneself from aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Please, let us move on to a specific topic, and I'm going to ask you specifically, did you take part in April, 1993, in an action or whatever I should call it, at the Sovici-Doljani -- in the Sovici-Doljani area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes. I did take part in the Sovici-Doljani action in April, 1993, with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Before you say everything you know about this to the Trial Chamber, could you please tell us who the overall commander was of this action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: The overall commander of this action was supposed to be the commander of the sector where this action was taking place. I think it was Mr. Siljeg who was then commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please now describe for the Trial Chamber what happened during that month of April in 1993, if you remember the actual dates please state them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Since a lot of time has gone by, I shall try to remember what I know. Our unit was stationed at the Heliodrom location in Mostar. In the early morning hours, our unit was told to be combat ready, about 2.00 a.m. Around 5.00 or 6.00, we received orders to go to the Sovicka Vrata region. When arriving in the Sovicka Vrata region, we encountered many units, some of which had already arrived there. Others were coming in then. There were members of the Posuska battalion, Posusje battalion, members of the Convicts Battalion, members of the Siroki Brijeg Brigade, and also there were some members of the HOS from Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at that site and approximately what time did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: We arrived somewhere around 8.00 in the morning. I established contact with the commander of the Posusje Battalion. They were already there. They wanted to establish contact with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I apologise to the witness for interrupting him but we don't have a date yet. As far as we have gotten so far is the month of April, 1993. If we could get a bit more specific on the date, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you told us that you will try your best to remember the specific date. Do you have any idea on what date this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would have come to that on my own, too. But I let the witness speak spontaneously. I let him tell his story. Of course this is a crucial question. If the witness remembers it, then I would have asked him but perhaps one should have some patience because after all, this is my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you arrived at Sovicka Vrata and then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I said that I established contact with the commander of the Posusje Battalion. He sent a platoon to establish contact with the checkpoint of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was a bit below Sovicka Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Vrata. While the members of the Posusje Battalion were moving towards this checkpoint, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina started firing at them, using mortar fire and small arms fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: They were operating against the locality where we were, around the school in Sovici. We determined the direction of the attack and then we, my unit, that is to say, and the Convicts Battalion, went in the direction of Pasije Stijene which is the most dominant feature in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: In the late afternoon hours, we took Pasije Stijene, that dominated above Sovici, and we continued this operation towards Bacina Planina, in the direction of Okajnica, Pisvir, feature 944, and we took that on the 19th in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: During these operations, we had two casualties. When we arrived at Kosna Luka we went down to the Doljani-Jablanica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You can speak a bit faster, Mr. Witness. You don't have it wait that long.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Then we established contact with the Convicts Battalion and they also had sustained one casualty, Mr. Boka Barbaric, that is. We helped them to get the dead body of Mr. Barbaric out. When we got the body, we actually completed the action. And we were supposed to go in the direction of Mostar where we were supposed to bury our dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did all of you leave, the entire ATG Baja Kraljevic and the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Both we and the Convicts Battalion left, in the afternoon, around 5.00 or 6.00, I can't remember exactly now, we left the area of Doljani and went in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you drive the dead bodies there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, to the best of your knowledge, did Mr. Naletilic have any role in these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic had no role in these events. I met Mr. Naletilic on the 19th, in the afternoon, on the road in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he leave the locality of Doljani together with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: That's where we met, and we talked, and Mr. Naletilic heard that his neighbour, Mr. Barbaric, was killed, and then, together with us, he went -- actually, he went right in front of my jeep. He went in the direction of Sovicka Vrata, in the direction of Siroki Brijeg. So he left Doljani. Upon arriving at Risovac, Mr. Naletilic, since he was going in front of me, stopped his jeep. We stopped there. We talked, and he went to pick up his children from Mr. Zelenika's at Risovac. That's where they had been. And I proceeded in the direction of Mostar. I was supposed to get my unit back to Heliodrom and to inform the families about the deaths of my two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. Tell me, please, can you say where you were or where your unit was, on the 8th or 5th or 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: On the 8th and on the 5th, or rather on the 8th of May, 1993, I was on the territory of Boksevica where I was wounded on the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, how many times were you wounded altogether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I was wounded four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is the most severe wound that you have, could you tell the Honourable Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: On the 12th of February, 1994, I was wounded the most seriously. That is when a shell exploded and wounded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know Ralf Rudiger

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, I know Mr. Ralf Rudiger while I was a member of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Baja Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No, Mr. Rudiger could not have been a member of Kraljevic because he did not meet the requirements to be a member of Baja Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, if you personally know about this, did Mr. Mladen Naletilic have any role or position in Mostar, Citluk, Posusje or Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic did not hold any position. I do not know of Mr. Naletilic being the deputy mayor of Siroki Brijeg --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, I do know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of a position he would have in Posusje or Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to look at a document, P206.1. Please read it. It has two -- rather three pages, and please tell me whether it corresponds to the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could the English version be put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Can you please look at the last page, the last page, please? Under item 4, the number of men, the strength, does this reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you whether there were any discussions about the Convicts Battalion being stationed at the Heliodrom. Was it ever there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: In 1992, the Convicts Battalion was supposed to be at one point, to be stationed at the Heliodrom, but it never was because it was not the nature of that unit to live in any barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, we will just take a moment to get these exhibits distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, can you come closer to the microphone when you speak? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just if there is any suspense, let me just tell the Chamber now, no intention or chance of completing by 1.45. I'm sure you understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we have to stop at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, Your Honour, but I will not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. complete my cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified a few moments ago that in approximately June, 1992, you were ordered to form the ATG Baja Kraljevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Towards the end of June, beginning of July, the Baja Kraljevic was formed and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say it was formed, when did it actually become operational? I would assume that something like that doesn't necessarily happen overnight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Let's say at the end of July or the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you said that the order to do this came from the HVO Main Staff. Can you be a bit more specific, if you can, do you recall the superior officer who ordered that this be done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I don't know who it was at the time. It may have been either Mr. Petkovic or Mr. Praljak but I can't say that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And at that time, did you understand any other -- excuse me, let me start again. Did you understand that there were any other professional units, so-called professional units, in the HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: At the time, there were no professional units. We were one of the first ones that were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There were a number of groups throughout the period 1992 to at least the end of 1993, were there not, which used the, as part of their name, used the words ATG, or the letters ATG, or the words anti-terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I don't know of any -- I know of the professional units that existed at the time. Those were the Baja Kraljevic ATG, that was -- and then the Bruno Busic professional unit, the Ludvig Pavlovic unit, and in 1993, I don't know whether the Convicts Battalion was a professional unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, my question is this: Isn't it true that there were a number of units in the HVO which used the term ATG? And I'll just -- if it assists you let me give you several names, if it will prompt your memory. The Benko Penavic ATG, the Vinko Skrobo ATG, the Zeljko Bosnjak ATG? Weren't there a number of units, sir, from sometime in 1992 and throughout 1993, that called themselves anti-terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, can you please break down your question? This question was too long for me. I cannot answer it in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were there other groups in the MVO military organisation which were called ATGs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I don't know. Not within the professional strength. Whether any other groups may have called themselves that, possibly, but these ATGs were under the home guard regiments, as far as I know, and they were attached to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me assist you, sir. It was never intended to be part of my question to limit you to professional units. I'm talking about anywhere within the HVO military structure, whether it was a home guard unit, whether it was a professional unit, whether it was a boy scout unit. Weren't there other organisations, units, within the HVO during this time that used the term ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, there were, of course there were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly asks the witness to come closer to the microphone. Otherwise, we won't be able to hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I gave you a couple of names a few moments ago, sir, can you please just assist the Chamber so that we can make sure again that we are speaking the same language so to speak, given the difficulty we've had in the last few minutes, can you name some of the other ATGs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I've heard of some ATGs, Vinko Skrobo, the Krusko ATG, and there were some other names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was commander of the Vinko Skrobo ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I think the commander of the Vinko Skrobo ATG was Mr. Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Also known as Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you really not know? Did you not operate with the Vinko Skrobo ATG at times and are you saying you have some doubt as to who the commanding officer was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes. I am not positive who the commander was, and we did not cooperate with that ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll come back to that probably on Monday. And who, sir, was the commanding officer of the Krusko ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I think that it was somebody they called Juka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you ever engage in any operations jointly with the Krusko unit under the command of Juka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No, never. I was never under Juka's command and I never participated in any operations with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, sir, again, I didn't ask you if you were under his command. I asked you did the -- your unit and his unit ever operate together or in the same operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've told the Judges that you received exclusively, I believe the word was, that you exclusively received your orders from the HVO Main Staff. Can you please tell the Judges who specifically -- I don't want to hide behind the term staff. Can you tell us the names of these officers who issued these orders directly to you or your unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this question is not correct. What does it mean, hide behind the term "staff" and what is the foundation for such an allegation, "to hide behind the staff"? What doe that imply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the question is important. As for other terminology, I don't think it's important. Maybe you could withdraw this kind of description.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: About hiding behind the term staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you said you received your orders from the HVO Main Staff. Can you please tell the Judges the individual officer from whom you received orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. Whoever was the duty operations officer Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could move my unit. I can't give you any individual names. I can't remember all the individual names. I can't tell you their names off my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, a few moments ago, you recalled in some detail events, for example, at Sovici-Doljani, even dates and times and who was driving in front of the other person. You're telling -- do you want this Chamber to understand that throughout the time of 1993, you do not know who was issuing orders to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Issues were -- orders were issued to us exclusively by the Main Staff but I can't remember the names of all the duty operations officers who worked in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, can you help us in this? Perhaps putting aside for the moment a duty officer, who were the very senior members of the HVO Main Staff who issued orders to you? Perhaps the issues -- excuse me, perhaps the orders were issued in their name. I understand that some duty officer might have been involved but who did you understand you were receiving orders from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: I think it was General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So should the Chamber understand from that, that in terms of what might be called command responsibility or superior responsibility, your position is that General Petkovic was responsible for you and your unit? Is that what you're telling the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've indicated in your testimony that this man Vukoja, was something like the commander on the ground, I think was counsel's term, for the Convicts Battalion during 1993. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vukoja --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the counsel did not say anything about Mr. Vukoja. I did not talk about Mr. Vukoja. Can my learned friend Mr. Scott ask correct questions? I know his cross-examination only too well, and this is what I'm asking him to do, to be correct in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, maybe Mr. Krsnik is offended by your phrase. I think it was "counsel's term."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll have Mr. Stringer check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In any event, sir, is it your testimony that this Vukoja was the ground commander of the Convicts Battalion in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: After the death of Mr. Marijan Hrkac, Cikota, Mr. Vukoja was the operations officer on the ground, the ground commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you operated on a number of occasions -- when I say, "You," I'm not going to ask your name but the Baja Kraljevic unit acted on a number of occasions jointly with the Convicts Battalion, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. We -- the last time we acted together was in Sovici and later on we may have come across each other in an area of responsibility, but we did not participate jointly in any operations after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, to your knowledge, did you know if Mr. Vukoja ever issued written orders to the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: He probably did, to his subordinate soldiers, but I don't know why he would do it in a written form.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, just, if you can remember, let me just ask you, this is probably my last question for today, do you remember in your -- the periods of your service in the HVO, do you remember ever seeing a written order from Mr. Vukoja to any soldier or member of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NQ
utterances.text: When Mr. Vukoja was the commander of the Convicts Battalion, I was not its member, so I don't know what documents did Mr. Vukoja issue to the members of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll stop there for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, yes? Well, Witness, I'm sorry that we have to keep you here in The Hague over the weekend. So I have to remind you, as I did to the other witnesses, that while you are still in The Hague, you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody or do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. We will continue on Monday morning. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll resume 9.00 on Monday morning in courtroom one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is it afternoon session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, 9.00 in Courtroom I.
